subject: Urgent: Inference timeouts impacting TheraHealth — initial notice & remediation plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@therahealth.com>; TheraHealth Ops <ops@therahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: [TheraHealth] Inference timeouts impacting production - immediate outreach

Hi Alicia / TheraHealth Ops team,

We’re seeing a rise in timeouts and 5xx errors for inference requests hitting your model pool in us-west-2 starting at ~15:30 UTC. Initial telemetry shows an increase in token-level error rates and occasional KV-cache misses that cascade into request failures. Severity: we’ve classified this as SEV-2 based on current impact (~2-3% request error rate).

Immediate actions we are taking now:
- Collecting a compact log bundle and KV cache snapshot (attaching shortly).
- Spinning up an isolated fallback pool to route a subset of traffic off the affected nodes.
- Planning a targeted mitigation (temporary disable of continuous batching for the affected pool) to prevent cache corruption; this will trade latency for success-rate.

We’d like permission to execute the mitigation at ~16:20 UTC (canary first, then full rollover) and to run a short restart of the worker containers in the affected pool if needed.

We’ll host a short war-room at the link below for live coordination — please join if your team is available: https://meet.redwood.com/incident/therahealth-0425 (10–15 minute check-in).

Attachments: system_logs_20270425.tar.gz (log bundle, 24MB) — will follow with KV snapshot.

Apologies for the disruption. We’ll send an executive-friendly summary within the hour and a scheduled postmortem invite for tomorrow.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [TheraHealth] Inference timeouts impacting production - immediate outreach

Thanks Tessa — we can confirm:
- Between 15:30–15:48 UTC, ~2% of production requests returned 502/504.
- The morning batch (06:00 PST) saw higher concurrency; customer-facing features served lower-quality responses during that window.

We’ll have two engineers on the call. Please include a short summary for our CTO (Marco Diaz) — he’ll be on standby and asked for an ETA.

Grant you permission to proceed with the canary mitigation at 16:20 UTC. Please keep us posted on expected change to latency.

— Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Ops, TheraHealth
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:58:00 +0000
Subject: FW: [TheraHealth] Inference timeouts impacting production - action items

Team — forwarding TheraHealth confirmation. Short tasking:
- David: lead the rollback/mitigation execution (canary then full). Coordinate container restarts only if canary shows improvement.
- Ben: run live diagnostics and own the customer-facing technical update (one-paragraph <= 5 lines plus ETA).
- Priyom: check autoscaler telemetry and reserve burst capacity if needed.
- Stephanie: draft an executive summary and a provisional credit proposal (they’ll likely ask about credits if postmortem shows service terms impact).

Plan: canary at 16:20 UTC (disable continuous batching on 10% of the pool, route 20% traffic). If errors drop to <0.5%, expand to 50% at 16:30, full at 16:45.

I’ll run the customer call and send the exec note once Ben confirms canary outcome.

— Tessa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: [TheraHealth] Inference timeouts impacting production - action items

Quick technical summary for the call and exec note:
- Root cause (preliminary): concurrent KV-cache invalidation when continuous batching combines high-token requests under a quantized kernel path. Under high concurrency the cache index can become inconsistent and trigger per-request failures.
- Immediate workaround: disable continuous batching for the affected pool and enable per-request routing for that model. This prevents the invalidation race; expected tradeoff is +30–60ms median latency for routed requests.
- Canary plan: disable batching on 2 nodes at 16:20 UTC for 20% of traffic, observe error rate and tail latency. If errors fall to <0.5% in 5m, proceed with wider rollout.

I’m attaching a lightweight KV snapshot we pulled prior to mitigation to help the postmortem: kvcache_snapshot_20270425.json.

If approved, I’ll execute the canary and post immediate results in this thread (+ join the call).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Engineering Liaison, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@therahealth.com>, Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@therahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: [TheraHealth] Incident update — executive summary & next steps

Hi Alicia / Marco,

Thanks again for the quick confirmation and for joining the call. Executive summary:
- What happened: a concurrency-related KV-cache invalidation bug under continuous batching caused a small fraction of inference requests in us-west-2 to fail between 15:30–15:48 UTC.
- Impact: ~2% of requests returned errors; we estimate a short-lived reduction in availability for affected endpoints. No exfiltration or data loss detected.
- What we did:
  • Deployed a canary mitigation at 16:20 UTC (disabled continuous batching on a subset) — errors dropped from ~2.3% to 0.2% within 4 minutes.
  • Rolled out the mitigation to the full affected pool by 16:40 UTC.
- Customer impact now: service restored to normal success rates; median latency increased by ~45ms for routed requests.

Next steps / commitments:
1) Postmortem: full written postmortem and remediation plan by 2027-04-26 18:00 UTC.
2) Follow-up meeting: 2027-04-26 17:00 UTC (60 min) — invite to follow.
3) Credits: provisional service credit offer equivalent to one day of average production usage while we investigate; we’ll refine after the postmortem.

For transparency, interim report: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/20270425-interim-report and ticket SUP-4319: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-4319.

If you’d like a deeper technical walkthrough on the postmortem call, Ben will lead that portion.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll take ownership of the follow-up and ensure a clear remediation timeline.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
